title: Whole-model Pocket/Adaptive2D with area offset or extension (and stock-source Adaptive) cut the part with no op finding and post on a turned stock

body:
**What happens:** whole-model 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive (and the stock-source Adaptive of #1554) can cut into the part with **no finding on the op**. On a **turned (rotated) stock** the post goes out, because the program sim refuses to judge a turned stock and nothing else catches it. Found by M5's review of PR #1597 (pullrequestreview-5899991928), on upstream main be27a4c7 plus #1597.

| Case | Depth into the part | Op findings | Aligned stock | Turned stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pocket / Adaptive2D, whole-model source, Area offset +3 | 4.0-4.25 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |
| Pocket / Adaptive2D, whole-model source, extension +5 | 5 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |
| #1554: stock-source Adaptive2D / Pocket | 7 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |

With default area controls (and containment On or Outside) these ops stay outside the part (worst clearance -0.005 mm). The gouge needs a positive area offset or extension, or a stock source.

**Why:** these ops carry `DepthLaw::None`, so the op itself never judges the cut against the model. `uncovered()` (crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged whatever its depth law, so when the program sim cannot model the stock (turned, posed, rotary), a None-law op that cuts the part goes to the post. Same root as #1595 (Engrave/Trace) and the TrochoidalSlot gap fixed by #1597. This is a gouge that passes on a turned stock: P1.

**Expected:** a whole-model or stock-source Pocket or Adaptive2D whose cut reaches into the part is refused on the op by name (a law that judges the region it actually cuts against the model), or at minimum `uncovered()` refuses to post a None-law op on a model source when the program sim cannot judge it. Legal whole-model pockets with default controls must still post. That is why #1597 did not simply make `uncovered()` refuse every None-law op.

**Done means:** the three rows above are refused (on the op, and the post is blocked) with the stock aligned and turned; legal whole-model pockets and adaptives with default controls still post on both. Pinned through `operation::generate` and the post, mutation-checked.

Related: #1595 (the same `uncovered()` question for Engrave/Trace), #1554 (stock-source Adaptive: not only verify-caught; it posts on a turned stock), #1593 / PR #1597, #1550.
